items.stem: Germany implemented a policy of unrestricted submarine warfare in 1917, announcing it would sink all ships — neutral or belligerent — in the war zone around Britain. Which of the following best evaluates Germany's strategic reasoning and its fatal flaw?
items.stemEs: Alemania implementó una política de guerra submarina irrestricta en 1917, anunciando que hundiría todos los barcos — neutrales o beligerantes — en la zona de guerra alrededor de Gran Bretaña. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor el razonamiento estratégico de Alemania y su error fatal?

choices.text: Germany gambled that submarines could force Britain to surrender before U.S. forces mobilized — an internally coherent strategy whose fatal flaw was underestimating how quickly American troops would arrive and affect the battlefield.
choices.textEs: Alemania apostó a que los submarinos podrían obligar a Gran Bretaña a rendirse antes de que las fuerzas de EE. UU. pudieran movilizarse — una estrategia internamente coherente cuyo error fatal fue subestimar con qué rapidez llegarían las fuerzas americanas y afectarían el campo de batalla.

choices.text: Germany implemented unrestricted submarine warfare without any coherent strategic reasoning, acting purely out of desperation and a desire to demonstrate continued military capability after years of grueling stalemate on the Western Front.
choices.textEs: Alemania implementó la guerra submarina irrestricta sin ningún razonamiento estratégico, puramente como un acto desesperado para demostrar capacidad militar.

choices.text: Germany implemented unrestricted submarine warfare with the genuine belief that the United States would never declare war regardless of the naval provocation, since domestic isolationism would prevent Wilson from taking military action.
choices.textEs: Alemania implementó la guerra submarina irrestricta creyendo que Estados Unidos nunca declararía la guerra independientemente de la provocación.

choices.text: Germany implemented unrestricted submarine warfare and it succeeded strategically in forcing Britain to begin serious peace negotiations before the United States had time to formally declare war and begin mobilizing forces.
choices.textEs: Alemania implementó la guerra submarina irrestricta y tuvo éxito al obligar a Gran Bretaña a buscar negociaciones de paz antes de que EE. UU. declarara la guerra.

items.explanation: Germany's strategic reasoning was internally coherent but contained a fatal flaw. Germany gambled that unrestricted submarine warfare could strangle British supply lines and force Britain out of the war before the United States could mobilize and deploy forces in significant numbers — essentially a race against time. German military planners calculated (correctly) that the U.S. would declare war in response, but believed (incorrectly) that they could deliver a knockout blow to Britain before American forces arrived in decisive numbers. The fatal flaw was underestimating American mobilization speed and overestimating the time it would take for U.S. forces to affect the battlefield. Options B and C misidentify the strategic logic; Option D is factually incorrect.
items.explanationEs: El razonamiento estratégico de Alemania era internamente coherente pero contenía un error fatal. Alemania apostó a que la guerra submarina irrestricta podría estrangular las líneas de suministro británicas y sacar a Gran Bretaña de la guerra antes de que Estados Unidos pudiera movilizar y desplegar fuerzas en números significativos — esencialmente una carrera contra el tiempo. El error fatal fue subestimar la velocidad de movilización americana y sobrestimar el tiempo que tardarían las fuerzas de EE. UU. en afectar el campo de batalla. Las opciones B y C identifican incorrectamente la lógica estratégica; la D es factualmente incorrecta.

items.stem: The Zimmermann Telegram (1917), in which Germany proposed a military alliance with Mexico against the United States, was a major factor in American entry into WWI. Which of the following best evaluates why this telegram was particularly effective as a catalyst for American intervention?

UU. en la Primera Guerra Mundial. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor por qué este telegrama fue particularmente efectivo como catalizador para la intervención americana?

choices.text: The telegram was galvanizing because it conclusively revealed that Germany had developed a sophisticated military intelligence and espionage network within the United States capable of coordinating large-scale industrial sabotage operations.
choices.textEs: El telegrama fue efectivo porque reveló que Alemania tenía una sofisticada red de espionaje dentro de Estados Unidos capaz de coordinar operaciones de sabotaje.

choices.text: The telegram was especially effective because the German Foreign Secretary publicly and explicitly admitted its complete authenticity in a parliamentary statement, permanently eliminating any possibility of German denial.
choices.textEs: El telegrama fue efectivo principalmente porque el Secretario de Relaciones Exteriores alemán admitió públicamente su autenticidad, eliminando cualquier posibilidad de negación.

choices.text: The telegram was especially galvanizing because it transformed WWI from an abstract European conflict into a direct territorial threat, proposing that Mexico reclaim southwestern U.S. states — making German hostility toward America impossible to deny.
choices.textEs: El telegrama fue especialmente galvanizador porque transformó la Primera Guerra Mundial de un conflicto europeo abstracto en una amenaza territorial directa para Estados Unidos, proponiendo que México reclamara estados del suroeste americano — haciendo la guerra inmediatamente personal y geográficamente próxima.

choices.text: The telegram was galvanizing because it provided the first credible evidence of German plans to deploy chemical weapons against American population centers, generating rapid and overwhelming public support for a declaration of war.
choices.textEs: El telegrama fue efectivo porque reveló los planes de Alemania de usar armas químicas contra las ciudades americanas, lo que generó un abrumador apoyo público para la guerra.

items.explanation: The Zimmermann Telegram was particularly effective because it transformed WWI from a distant European conflict into an immediate threat to U.S. territory and sovereignty. Unlike the sinking of merchant ships — which threatened American lives and principles — the Telegram threatened American soil by proposing that Mexico recover Texas, New Mexico, and Arizona. This shift from abstract to concrete territorial threat was uniquely galvanizing, especially in the American West and South. It also undermined the remaining argument for neutrality by demonstrating that Germany actively sought to harm the continental United States, not just challenge American shipping rights. Options A and B identify secondary factors; Option D misidentifies the telegram's primary emotional impact.
items.explanationEs: El Telegrama Zimmermann fue particularmente efectivo porque transformó la Primera Guerra Mundial de un conflicto europeo distante en una amenaza inmediata para el territorio y la soberanía de EE. UU. A diferencia del hundimiento de barcos mercantes — que amenazaba las vidas y los principios americanos — el Telegrama amenazaba el suelo americano al proponer que México recuperara Texas, Nuevo México y Arizona. Este cambio de amenaza abstracta a concreta fue particularmente galvanizador. Las opciones A y B identifican factores secundarios; la D identifica incorrectamente el impacto emocional principal del telegrama.

choices.text: Democratic idealism had no role whatsoever in U.S. entry because Wilson was exclusively and transparently motivated by the need to protect the massive American financial investments in Allied war bonds and commercial loans.
choices.textEs: El idealismo democrático no tuvo ningún papel en la entrada de EE. UU. porque Wilson estaba motivado exclusivamente por proteger las inversiones financieras americanas en el esfuerzo bélico aliado.

choices.text: Wilson's idealistic justification reflected his genuine worldview but also provided inspiring public framing for what were simultaneously strategic and economic necessities — including protecting American commerce and financial investments in Allied victory.
choices.textEs: La justificación idealista de Wilson reflejó su cosmovisión genuina pero también proporcionó un enmarcamiento público inspirador para lo que eran simultáneamente necesidades estratégicas y económicas — las amenazas de la guerra submarina, las inversiones financieras en la victoria aliada y el Telegrama Zimmermann apuntaban todos hacia la intervención independientemente del idealismo democrático.

items.explanation: Wilson's idealistic rhetoric and the realpolitik factors were not mutually exclusive, but historians have identified a gap between them. The concrete drivers of U.S. entry were: unrestricted submarine warfare threatening American lives and shipping, the Zimmermann Telegram threatening U.S. territory, the massive financial investment American banks had in Allied victory (J.P. Morgan loans), and the strategic calculation that an Allied defeat would be catastrophic for U.S. interests. Wilson's 'make the world safe for democracy' framing was ideologically true to his worldview but also served as a more inspiring and politically useful justification than 'protect our loans to Britain.' The two coexisted, with ideology providing the public framing for strategically necessary action. Options A and B are too simplistic; Option C dismisses Wilson's genuine idealism.
items.explanationEs: La retórica idealista de Wilson y los factores de realpolitik no eran mutuamente excluyentes, pero los historiadores han identificado una brecha entre ellos. Los impulsores concretos de la entrada de EE. UU. fueron: la guerra submarina irrestricta que amenazaba vidas y envíos americanos, el Telegrama Zimmermann, la enorme inversión financiera de los bancos americanos en la victoria aliada y el cálculo estratégico de que una derrota aliada sería catastrófica. Las opciones A y B son demasiado simplistas; la C descarta el idealismo genuino de Wilson.

items.stem: American banks, particularly J.P. Morgan & Co., had loaned over $2 billion to the Allied powers by 1917. Which of the following best analyzes how these financial ties influenced the decision for U.S. entry into WWI?
items.stemEs: Los bancos americanos, particularmente J.P. Morgan & Co., habían prestado más de $2 mil millones a las potencias aliadas para 1917. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones analiza mejor cómo estos lazos financieros influyeron en la decisión de entrada de EE. UU. en la Primera Guerra Mundial?

choices.text: Financial ties to the Allied powers were the sole determining cause of U.S. entry into WWI because American bankers directly controlled and dictated President Wilson's foreign policy decision-making process throughout the neutrality period.
choices.textEs: Los lazos financieros fueron la única causa de la entrada de EE. UU. en la Primera Guerra Mundial porque los banqueros americanos controlaban directamente las decisiones de política exterior de Wilson.

choices.text: Financial ties created a powerful structural incentive for U.S. entry by giving American institutions a direct stake in Allied victory and increasing political pressure on Wilson to protect those investments from a German win.
choices.textEs: Los lazos financieros crearon un poderoso incentivo estructural para la entrada de EE. UU. al dar a las instituciones financieras americanas un interés directo en la victoria aliada, haciendo que una victoria alemana fuera potencialmente catastrófica para la economía de EE. UU. y aumentando la presión política para proteger esas inversiones.

choices.text: Financial ties between American institutions and the Allied powers had no significant influence on U.S. entry because Wilson consistently refused to consider any economic factors in making his war decision, relying solely on legal and moral reasoning.
choices.textEs: Los lazos financieros no tuvieron influencia significativa en la entrada de EE. UU. porque Wilson se negó a considerar factores económicos en su decisión de guerra.

choices.text: Financial ties caused the war indirectly by motivating American banks to secretly encourage Germany to resume unrestricted submarine warfare, which would then provide the necessary legal and political justification for U.S. entry to protect Allied loans.
choices.textEs: Los lazos financieros causaron la guerra al motivar a los bancos americanos a alentar secretamente a Alemania a usar la guerra submarina, lo que justificaría la entrada de EE. UU. para proteger los préstamos aliados.

items.explanation: The massive financial entanglement created a powerful structural incentive for U.S. entry: if Germany won the war, Allied nations might be unable to repay their enormous loans to American banks, potentially causing a financial crisis in the U.S. This did not mean financiers 'caused' the war decision directly — the decision was Wilson's and involved multiple factors — but it created a financial community that had a direct stake in Allied victory and the political influence to make that stake felt. It also meant that 'neutral' American trade was overwhelmingly with the Allies, since the British blockade prevented trade with Germany. Options A and C are oversimplifications; Option D misidentifies the mechanism of influence.
items.explanationEs: El enorme enredo financiero creó un poderoso incentivo estructural para la entrada de EE. UU.: si Alemania ganaba la guerra, las naciones aliadas podrían no poder pagar sus enormes préstamos a los bancos americanos. Esto no significó que los financieros 'causaran' directamente la decisión de guerra, pero creó una comunidad financiera con un interés directo en la victoria aliada y la influencia política para hacer sentir ese interés. Las opciones A y C son simplificaciones excesivas; la D identifica incorrectamente el mecanismo de influencia.

items.stem: Wilson asked Congress to declare war in April 1917, citing Germany's unrestricted submarine warfare, the Zimmermann Telegram, and the need to defend democracy. Which of the following best evaluates the relative importance of these factors in actually determining the timing of U.S. intervention?
items.stemEs: Wilson pidió al Congreso que declarara la guerra en abril de 1917, citando la guerra submarina irrestricta de Alemania, el Telegrama Zimmermann y la necesidad de defender la democracia. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor la importancia relativa de estos factores para determinar realmente el momento de la intervención de EE. UU.?

choices.text: The democratic idealism argument was the most decisive factor, since Wilson could not have secured congressional approval without the inspirational Wilsonian framing.
choices.textEs: El argumento de la defensa de la democracia fue el factor más decisivo porque Wilson no podría haber obtenido la aprobación del Congreso sin el enmarcamiento idealista.

choices.text: The Zimmermann Telegram was the most decisive factor because it provided the first concrete, undeniable evidence of German hostile intent toward the United States.
choices.textEs: El Telegrama Zimmermann fue el factor más decisivo porque fue la primera evidencia concreta de hostilidad alemana hacia Estados Unidos.

choices.text: Germany's permanent resumption of unrestricted submarine warfare in February 1917 was the decisive timing factor, removing the diplomatic ambiguity that had allowed Wilson to maintain neutrality.
choices.textEs: La reanudación permanente de la guerra submarina irrestricta por parte de Alemania en febrero de 1917 fue el factor de tiempo más decisivo porque eliminó la ambigüedad diplomática que había permitido a Wilson mantener la neutralidad, sin dejarle otra opción que salvar el honor más que la guerra.

choices.text: All three factors were equally decisive, and the declaration of war could not have occurred without all three events happening in close sequence.
choices.textEs: Los tres factores fueron igualmente decisivos y la guerra no podría haber comenzado sin que los tres ocurrieran simultáneamente.

items.explanation: The resumption of unrestricted submarine warfare in February 1917 was the most decisive timing factor. Germany had previously backed down (Sussex Pledge, 1916) under American pressure, but in 1917 committed to the policy permanently — a clear statement that Germany would no longer respect American neutral rights regardless of consequences. This left Wilson with no face-saving diplomatic option. The Zimmermann Telegram, revealed in March 1917, amplified public outrage and eliminated the remaining political opposition to intervention. The defense of democracy argument provided the moral framework. But the concrete, immediate trigger was Germany's unambiguous announcement that it would sink American ships — removing the diplomatic ambiguity that had allowed Wilson to maintain neutrality. Options A and B elevate secondary factors; Option D misidentifies the sequencing.
items.explanationEs: La reanudación de la guerra submarina irrestricta en febrero de 1917 fue el factor de tiempo más decisivo. Alemania se había retirado previamente (Promesa del Sussex, 1916) bajo presión americana, pero en 1917 se comprometió con la política permanentemente — una declaración clara de que Alemania ya no respetaría los derechos neutrales americanos. El Telegrama Zimmermann, revelado en marzo de 1917, amplificó la indignación pública. Pero el detonante concreto e inmediato fue el anuncio inequívoco de Alemania de que hundiría los barcos americanos. Las opciones A y B elevan factores secundarios; la D identifica incorrectamente la secuencia.

items.stem: Some historians argue that the United States entered WWI primarily for economic reasons — to protect loans and trade with the Allies. Other historians argue that genuine democratic idealism was the primary motivation. Which of the following presents the most defensible synthesis of these competing interpretations?
items.stemEs: Algunos historiadores argumentan que Estados Unidos entró en la Primera Guerra Mundial principalmente por razones económicas — para proteger préstamos y comercio con los Aliados. Otros historiadores argumentan que el idealismo democrático genuino fue la motivación principal. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones presenta la síntesis más defendible de estas interpretaciones en competencia?

choices.text: Economic entanglement and democratic idealism were mutually reinforcing: financial interests created structural pressure toward Allied victory while ideological commitments made that outcome morally desirable, making both explanations necessary.
choices.textEs: El enredo económico y el idealismo democrático no eran explicaciones en competencia sino factores mutuamente reforzantes: los intereses financieros crearon presión estructural hacia la victoria aliada mientras que los compromisos ideológicos hacían que ese resultado fuera moralmente deseable, con ambos operando simultáneamente en la toma de decisiones de Wilson.

choices.text: Economic interests were the only real and historically verifiable cause of U.S. entry into WWI; Wilson's democratic idealism was entirely manufactured political rhetoric with no genuine connection to the actual motivations driving U.S. policy.
choices.textEs: Los intereses económicos fueron la única causa real de la entrada de EE. UU.; el idealismo democrático fue retórica completamente fabricada sin conexión con las motivaciones reales de política.

choices.text: Democratic idealism was the only authentic cause of U.S. entry into the war; economic interests in Allied loan repayment and commercial access were completely irrelevant to Wilson's actual foreign policy decision-making process.
choices.textEs: El idealismo democrático fue la única causa real de la entrada de EE. UU.; los intereses económicos fueron irrelevantes para el proceso real de toma de decisiones de Wilson.

choices.text: Neither economic interests nor democratic idealism adequately explains U.S. entry into WWI; the war was caused entirely by the Zimmermann Telegram as an unpredictable and singular diplomatic incident that forced Wilson's hand.
choices.textEs: Ni los intereses económicos ni el idealismo democrático explican la entrada de EE. UU.; la guerra fue causada enteramente por el Telegrama Zimmermann como un evento singular e impredecible.

items.explanation: The most defensible synthesis acknowledges that economic interests and democratic idealism were not competing explanations that cancel each other out, but complementary factors that reinforced each other. The economic entanglement created a structural incentive toward Allied victory, while the ideological framing made that outcome morally desirable. Wilson himself appeared to genuinely believe in both — he did not fake his democratic idealism, and he was also aware of the economic stakes. Moreover, the specific trigger (submarine warfare) was a genuine affront to American neutral rights and democratic principles, not merely an economic inconvenience. The most defensible position is that multiple causes, converging over time, made U.S. entry both economically necessary and ideologically justified — with each reinforcing the other. Options B, C, and D each present monocausal explanations that the historical evidence does not support.
items.explanationEs: La síntesis más defendible reconoce que los intereses económicos y el idealismo democrático no eran explicaciones en competencia que se cancelan mutuamente, sino factores complementarios que se reforzaban mutuamente. El enredo económico creó un incentivo estructural hacia la victoria aliada, mientras que el enmarcamiento ideológico hizo que ese resultado fuera moralmente deseable. Wilson mismo parecía creer genuinamente en ambos. Las opciones B, C y D presentan explicaciones monocausales que la evidencia histórica no respalda.

items.stem: Congress passed the Espionage Act (1917) and Sedition Act (1918) to suppress dissent during WWI. Which of the following best evaluates the relationship between U.S. entry into WWI and the restriction of civil liberties at home?
items.stemEs: El Congreso aprobó la Ley de Espionaje (1917) y la Ley de Sedición (1918) para suprimir la disidencia durante la Primera Guerra Mundial. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor la relación entre la entrada de EE. UU. en la Primera Guerra Mundial y la restricción de las libertades civiles en casa?

choices.text: There was no significant relationship between U.S. war entry and civil liberties restrictions; the Espionage and Sedition Acts were entirely unrelated to the war and were driven by domestic concerns about labor radicalism predating American involvement.
choices.textEs: No hubo una relación significativa; las restricciones a las libertades civiles fueron completamente ajenas a la entrada de EE. UU. en la guerra y fueron impulsadas por preocupaciones domésticas no relacionadas.

choices.text: U.S. entry into WWI actually caused the expansion and strengthening of civil liberties because the democratic ideology Wilson used to justify intervention also reinforced constitutional free speech protections in subsequent judicial decisions.
choices.textEs: La entrada de EE. UU. en la Primera Guerra Mundial causó la expansión de las libertades civiles porque la ideología democrática utilizada para justificar la guerra también fortaleció las protecciones de la libertad de expresión.

choices.text: The Espionage and Sedition Acts were purely defensive national security measures that were narrowly applied and never resulted in any significant prosecution of American citizens for political speech or antiwar organizing activities.
choices.textEs: Las Leyes de Espionaje y Sedición fueron medidas puramente defensivas de seguridad que nunca resultaron en enjuiciamientos significativos de ciudadanos americanos.

choices.text: U.S. entry into WWI created a fundamental paradox: the government suppressed domestic dissent through the Espionage and Sedition Acts while simultaneously fighting abroad for democratic values, showing that wartime security imperatives consistently strain civil liberties commitments.
choices.textEs: La entrada de EE. UU. en la Primera Guerra Mundial creó una paradoja: el gobierno suprimió la disidencia doméstica a través de las Leyes de Espionaje y Sedición mientras luchaba simultáneamente en el extranjero por los valores democráticos — demostrando que los imperativos de seguridad nacional en tiempos de guerra anulan constantemente los compromisos de libertades civiles.

items.explanation: The relationship is not coincidental: wars historically create conditions in which governments restrict civil liberties by claiming that dissent threatens national security. The U.S. entry into WWI on idealistic democratic grounds made the suppression of anti-war dissent particularly paradoxical — the government was fighting for democracy abroad while curtailing free speech at home. The prosecution of Eugene Debs (Socialist Party leader) for an anti-war speech illustrates this tension directly. This pattern — war as pretext for civil liberties restrictions — would recur in American history (Red Scare, WWII Japanese internment, etc.). Options A and B are oversimplifications; Option C ignores the documented suppressions that occurred.
items.explanationEs: La relación no es coincidente: las guerras históricamente crean condiciones en las que los gobiernos restringen las libertades civiles afirmando que la disidencia amenaza la seguridad nacional. La entrada de EE. UU. en la Primera Guerra Mundial por motivos democráticos idealistas hizo que la supresión de la disidencia anti-guerra fuera particularmente paradójica — el gobierno luchaba por la democracia en el extranjero mientras recortaba la libertad de expresión en casa. La persecución de Eugene Debs ilustra esta tensión directamente. Las opciones A y B son simplificaciones excesivas; la C ignora las supresiones documentadas que ocurrieron.

items.stem: The United States entered WWI as an 'Associated Power' rather than an Allied Power. Which of the following best explains the significance of this distinction and what it reveals about Wilson's vision for the post-war world?
items.stemEs: Estados Unidos entró en la Primera Guerra Mundial como 'Potencia Asociada' en lugar de como Potencia Aliada. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor la importancia de esta distinción y qué revela sobre la visión de Wilson para el mundo de posguerra?

choices.text: The designation had no real significance because 'Associated Power' and 'Allied Power' were interchangeable terms used solely for diplomatic protocol.
choices.textEs: La designación no tuvo ninguna importancia real porque 'Potencia Asociada' y 'Potencia Aliada' eran términos intercambiables usados únicamente para el protocolo diplomático.

choices.text: By designating the U.S. an 'Associated Power,' Wilson asserted independence from Allied war aims and secret treaties, preserving the moral authority to impose a different peace
choices.textEs: Al designar a EE. UU. como 'Potencia Asociada', Wilson afirmó la independencia de los objetivos de guerra y los tratados secretos aliados, preservando la autoridad moral para imponer una paz diferente — presagiando su conflicto con Gran Bretaña y Francia en la Conferencia de Paz de París sobre las anexiones territoriales que contradecían sus Catorce Puntos.

choices.text: The designation proved that Wilson did not actually support the Allied war effort and was secretly working toward a negotiated peace with Germany.
choices.textEs: La designación demostró que Wilson en realidad no apoyaba el esfuerzo bélico aliado y estaba trabajando en secreto hacia una paz negociada con Alemania.

choices.text: The designation required the United States to contribute military forces only in defensive operations rather than offensive campaigns, limiting American military involvement.
choices.textEs: La designación requirió que Estados Unidos contribuyera fuerzas militares solo en operaciones defensivas en lugar de campañas ofensivas, limitando la participación militar americana.

items.explanation: By designating the United States an 'Associated Power' rather than a formal Ally, Wilson was asserting U.S. independence from the specific war aims, secret treaties, and imperial ambitions of Britain and France. He wanted to preserve the moral authority to impose a different — more idealistic — peace settlement rather than being bound by Allied war aims. This foreshadowed his conflict with Britain and France at the Paris Peace Conference (1919), where he discovered that the Allies' secret treaties (Sykes-Picot, Treaty of London) committed them to territorial annexations that contradicted his Fourteen Points. The distinction was Wilson's attempt to maintain the high ground as a disinterested mediator rather than a participant in European imperial politics. Options A and C misidentify the significance; Option D is factually inaccurate.
items.explanationEs: Al designar a Estados Unidos como 'Potencia Asociada' en lugar de Aliado formal, Wilson estaba afirmando la independencia de EE. UU. de los objetivos de guerra específicos, los tratados secretos y las ambiciones imperiales de Gran Bretaña y Francia. Quería preservar la autoridad moral para imponer un acuerdo de paz diferente — más idealista — en lugar de estar vinculado por los objetivos de guerra aliados. Esto presagió su conflicto con Gran Bretaña y Francia en la Conferencia de Paz de París (1919). Las opciones A y C identifican incorrectamente el significado; la D es factualmente inexacta.

items.stem: Congress passed the Selective Service Act (1917) to draft American men into the military. Which of the following best evaluates the significance of this decision for how WWI changed the relationship between the federal government and American citizens?
items.stemEs: El Congreso aprobó la Ley de Servicio Selectivo (1917) para reclutar a hombres americanos en el ejército. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor la importancia de esta decisión para cómo la Primera Guerra Mundial cambió la relación entre el gobierno federal y los ciudadanos americanos?

choices.text: The Selective Service Act dramatically expanded federal power by establishing the government's authority to compel military service from citizens, setting a precedent that wars could justify sweeping claims on individual liberty.
choices.textEs: La Ley de Servicio Selectivo amplió dramáticamente el poder federal al establecer la autoridad del gobierno para obligar el servicio militar a los ciudadanos, sentando un precedente de que las guerras podían justificar amplias reclamaciones sobre la libertad individual y que el gobierno federal podía movilizar la sociedad a escala masiva.

choices.text: The Selective Service Act had minimal historical significance because the United States had used military conscription in every major war since the Civil War, making WWI no different in its relationship between citizen and federal government.
choices.textEs: La Ley de Servicio Selectivo tuvo una importancia mínima porque EE. UU. siempre había utilizado el servicio obligatorio en sus grandes guerras, haciendo que la Primera Guerra Mundial no fuera diferente de los conflictos anteriores.

choices.text: The Selective Service Act weakened federal governmental authority by generating such massive popular resistance, legal challenges, and draft evasion that it significantly undermined the overall efficiency of the American war effort.
choices.textEs: La Ley de Servicio Selectivo debilitó al gobierno federal al crear una resistencia popular masiva que socavó el esfuerzo bélico.

choices.text: The Selective Service Act was ultimately unnecessary because sufficient numbers of American volunteers had already enlisted to meet the military's manpower needs, making compulsory conscription administratively redundant.
choices.textEs: La Ley de Servicio Selectivo fue innecesaria porque suficientes voluntarios ya se habían alistado para satisfacer las necesidades militares de EE. UU. sin servicio obligatorio.

items.explanation: The Selective Service Act represented a major expansion of federal power over individuals: the government now asserted the authority to compel military service from male citizens, regardless of their personal views on the war. This was unprecedented at the scale used in WWI and established that the federal government could make sweeping demands on individual citizens in wartime. Combined with war financing (Liberty Bonds, income tax) and economic regulation (War Industries Board), WWI dramatically expanded the reach of the federal government in American life — a precedent for the even greater expansion in WWII and the New Deal era. Options B and C misidentify the significance; Option D presents an inaccurate historical counterfactual.
items.explanationEs: La Ley de Servicio Selectivo representó una importante expansión del poder federal sobre los individuos: el gobierno ahora afirmaba la autoridad de obligar el servicio militar a los ciudadanos varones, independientemente de sus opiniones personales sobre la guerra. Esto fue sin precedentes a la escala utilizada en la Primera Guerra Mundial y estableció que el gobierno federal podía hacer demandas importantes a los ciudadanos individuales en tiempos de guerra. Combinado con el financiamiento de guerra y la regulación económica, la Primera Guerra Mundial expandió dramáticamente el alcance del gobierno federal en la vida americana. Las opciones B y C identifican incorrectamente el significado; la D presenta un contrafactual histórico inexacto.

items.stem: The Russian Revolution of 1917 and Russia's withdrawal from WWI had significant implications for American entry into the war. Which of the following best analyzes how the Russian Revolution affected the ideological case Wilson was making for American intervention?
items.stemEs: La Revolución Rusa de 1917 y la retirada de Rusia de la Primera Guerra Mundial tuvieron implicaciones significativas para la entrada de EE. UU. en la guerra. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones analiza mejor cómo la Revolución Rusa afectó el caso ideológico que Wilson estaba haciendo para la intervención americana?

choices.text: The Russian Revolution significantly weakened Wilson's case for American intervention because the removal of the Czar made it more difficult to argue convincingly that Germany, rather than revolutionary Russia, was the primary threat to democratic governance.
choices.textEs: La Revolución Rusa debilitó el caso de Wilson para la intervención porque la eliminación del Zar dificultó el argumento de que Alemania era la principal amenaza para el gobierno democrático.

choices.text: The Russian Revolution had absolutely no effect on Wilson's public case for intervention because it occurred after the United States had already formally declared war on Germany and was therefore entirely irrelevant to the original decision.
choices.textEs: La Revolución Rusa no tuvo ningún efecto en el caso de Wilson porque ocurrió después de que EE. UU. declarara la guerra y por lo tanto fue irrelevante para la decisión.

choices.text: The February Revolution's removal of the autocratic Czar actually strengthened Wilson's case by allowing him to frame the Allies as genuinely democratic powers fighting German militarism, eliminating the embarrassment of defending autocratic Russia as a democracy partner.
choices.textEs: La eliminación del Zar autocrático por la Revolución de Febrero de la coalición aliada en realidad fortaleció el caso de Wilson al permitirle enmarcar a los Aliados como potencias genuinamente democráticas que luchan contra el militarismo alemán, sin la vergüenza de defender a la Rusia autocrática como socio democrático.

choices.text: The Russian Revolution was the decisive factor that convinced Wilson to enter the war primarily to contain the spread of Bolshevism westward into Central Europe rather than to defend liberal democracy against German militarism.
choices.textEs: La Revolución Rusa convenció a Wilson de entrar en la guerra principalmente para prevenir la propagación del bolchevismo en lugar de defender la democracia contra Alemania.

items.explanation: The Russian Revolution's February (March) 1917 phase actually strengthened Wilson's ideological case. The removal of the Czar — an autocratic monarch — from the Allied coalition made it easier to argue that the Allies were genuinely fighting for democracy against German militarism. Previously, having autocratic Russia as an ally had complicated the 'war for democracy' argument. The Bolshevik Revolution in October/November 1917 then complicated matters further, but Wilson's war message in April 1917 came after the February revolution and before the Bolshevik takeover. Option A reverses the ideological impact; Option B misidentifies the timeline; Option D mischaracterizes Wilson's reasoning.
items.explanationEs: La fase de febrero (marzo) de 1917 de la Revolución Rusa en realidad fortaleció el caso ideológico de Wilson. La eliminación del Zar — un monarca autocrático — de la coalición aliada facilitó el argumento de que los Aliados estaban genuinamente luchando por la democracia contra el militarismo alemán. La opción A invierte el impacto ideológico; la B identifica incorrectamente la cronología; la D caracteriza incorrectamente el razonamiento de Wilson.

items.stem: President Wilson claimed that American entry into WWI was not driven by national self-interest but by a disinterested commitment to international law and democratic values. Which of the following best evaluates the credibility of this claim?
items.stemEs: El Presidente Wilson afirmó que la entrada de EE. UU. en la Primera Guerra Mundial no fue impulsada por el interés propio nacional sino por un compromiso desinteresado con el derecho internacional y los valores democráticos. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor la credibilidad de esta afirmación?

choices.text: Wilson's claim was fully credible because the United States had no national interests at stake in WWI and entered purely to serve international law.
choices.textEs: La afirmación de Wilson era completamente creíble porque Estados Unidos no tenía intereses nacionales en juego en la Primera Guerra Mundial y entró puramente para servir al derecho internacional.

choices.text: Wilson's claim was entirely not credible because the United States entered exclusively to protect its financial investments in the Allied war effort.
choices.textEs: La afirmación de Wilson era completamente indigna de crédito porque Estados Unidos entró exclusivamente para proteger sus inversiones financieras en el esfuerzo bélico aliado.

choices.text: Wilson's claim was partially credible — he genuinely believed in democratic values and international law — but overstated, because national interests were deeply interwoven with the idealistic justifications he offered.
choices.textEs: La afirmación de Wilson era parcialmente creíble — él genuinamente creía en los valores democráticos y el derecho internacional — pero exagerada, porque los intereses nacionales (enredo financiero, preocupaciones estratégicas, ventajas comerciales) estaban profundamente entrelazados con las justificaciones idealistas que ofreció.

choices.text: Wilson's claim was entirely not credible because he had no genuine personal commitment to democratic values and was purely a cynical political actor.
choices.textEs: La afirmación de Wilson era completamente indigna de crédito porque no tenía ningún compromiso personal genuino con los valores democráticos y era puramente un actor político cínico.

items.explanation: Wilson's claim of disinterested altruism was partially credible but significantly overstated. There is good evidence that Wilson genuinely believed in democratic values and international law — his Fourteen Points were not cynical inventions. However, the claim of disinterested national action is undermined by: the massive financial entanglement of American banks in Allied victory, the strategic threat of a German-dominated Europe to U.S. interests, the specific protective value of Allied naval supremacy for U.S. commerce, and Wilson's own admission that a German victory would be dangerous for the United States. Self-interest and idealism were intertwined, not separable. Claiming pure altruism was both politically useful and historically inaccurate. Options A and B are oversimplifications; Option D dismisses Wilson's genuine idealism.
items.explanationEs: La afirmación de altruismo desinteresado de Wilson era parcialmente creíble pero significativamente exagerada. Hay buena evidencia de que Wilson genuinamente creía en los valores democráticos y el derecho internacional. Sin embargo, la afirmación de acción nacional desinteresada está socavada por: el enorme enredo financiero de los bancos americanos en la victoria aliada, la amenaza estratégica de una Europa dominada por Alemania para los intereses de EE. UU., etc. Las opciones A y B son simplificaciones excesivas; la D descarta el idealismo genuino de Wilson.

items.stem:
Read the following excerpt from President Woodrow Wilson's Address to Congress Requesting a Declaration of War, April 2, 1917 (Bryan, William Jennings, ed., Republic or Empire (1899), public domain — public domain):

"It is a fearful thing to lead this great peaceful people into war, into the most disastrous and dismal of all wars, civilization itself seeming to be in the balance. Pero el derecho es más precioso que la paz, y lucharemos por las cosas que siempre hemos llevado más cerca de nuestros corazones — por la democracia, por el derecho de quienes se someten a la autoridad de tener voz en sus propios gobiernos, por los derechos y libertades de las pequeñas naciones, por un dominio universal del derecho por tal concierto de pueblos libres que traiga paz y seguridad a todas las naciones y haga al mundo mismo finalmente libre."

Document-Based Question: The Road to War — American Neutrality and Entry into World War I, 1914–1917

Directions: Read the three documents below. Then write a well-organized essay addressing the following question: To what extent was U.S. entry into World War I in April 1917 a response to deliberate foreign provocation versus a product of the United States' own prior choices and entanglements?

Your essay must:
— Apply SOAPS analysis to at least two documents
— Use evidence from all three documents
— Incorporate outside knowledge of U.S. neutrality policy 1914–1917
— Construct a clear, defensible argument

---
DOCUMENT 1
The Zimmermann Telegram, January 16, 1917 — U.S. National Archives, public domain (decoded and released by British intelligence to the U.S. State Department, February 24, 1917):
"We intend to begin on the first of February unrestricted submarine warfare. We shall endeavor in spite of this to keep the United States of America neutral. In the event of this not succeeding, we make Mexico the following offer to alliance on the following basis: make war together, make peace together, generous financial support and an understanding on our part that Mexico is to reconquer the lost territory in Texas, New Mexico, and Arizona. The settlement in detail is left to you. You will inform the President of the above most secretly as soon as the outbreak of war with the United States is certain..."
— Arthur Zimmermann, German Foreign Secretary

---
DOCUMENT 2
President Woodrow Wilson, Address to Congress Requesting Declaration of War, April 2, 1917 — Bryan, William Jennings, ed., Republic or Empire (1899), public domain, public domain:
"The present German submarine warfare against commerce is a warfare against mankind. It is a war against all nations. American ships have been sunk, American lives taken, in ways which it has stirred us very deeply to learn of, but the ships and people of other neutral and friendly nations have been sunk and overwhelmed in the waters in the same way. There has been no discrimination. The challenge is to all mankind."

---
DOCUMENT 3
Senator George Norris of Nebraska, Speech Opposing U.S. Declaration of War, April 4, 1917 — Bryan, William Jennings, ed., Republic or Empire (1899), public domain, public domain:
"We are going into war upon the command of gold... I feel that we are about to put the dollar sign on the American flag... I am confident that the object of the President, in asking for war, is to serve the wealthy interests of our country and not the plain people... I think we should wait patiently until the American people are willing to go into war for their country rather than for the bankers."
items.stemEs:
Pregunta Basada en Documentos: El Camino a la Guerra — Neutralidad de EE. UU. y Entrada en la Primera Guerra Mundial, 1914–1917

Instrucciones: Lea los tres documentos a continuación. Luego escriba un ensayo bien organizado que aborde la siguiente pregunta: ¿En qué medida fue la entrada de EE. UU. en la Primera Guerra Mundial en abril de 1917 una respuesta a la provocación extranjera deliberada versus un producto de las propias elecciones y compromisos previos de los Estados Unidos?

Su ensayo debe:
— Aplicar el análisis SOAPS a al menos dos documentos
— Utilizar evidencia de los tres documentos
— Incorporar conocimiento externo de la política de neutralidad de EE. UU. 1914–1917
— Construir un argumento claro y defendible

---
DOCUMENTO 1
El Telegrama Zimmermann, 16 de enero de 1917 — Archivos Nacionales de EE. UU., dominio público (decodificado y entregado por la inteligencia británica al Departamento de Estado de EE. UU., 24 de febrero de 1917):
"Tenemos la intención de comenzar el primero de febrero la guerra submarina sin restricciones. Nos esforzaremos a pesar de esto en mantener a los Estados Unidos de América neutrales. En caso de que esto no tenga éxito, hacemos a México la siguiente oferta de alianza sobre las siguientes bases: hacer la guerra juntos, hacer la paz juntos, apoyo financiero generoso y entendimiento de nuestra parte de que México recobre el territorio perdido en Texas, Nuevo México y Arizona. El arreglo en detalle se lo dejamos a usted. Informará al Presidente de lo anterior de la manera más secreta tan pronto como el estallido de la guerra con los Estados Unidos sea seguro..."
— Arthur Zimmermann, Secretario de Relaciones Exteriores alemán

---
DOCUMENTO 2
Presidente Woodrow Wilson, Discurso al Congreso Solicitando Declaración de Guerra, 2 de abril de 1917 — Registro del Congreso de EE. UU., dominio público:
"La actual guerra submarina alemana contra el comercio es una guerra contra la humanidad. Es una guerra contra todas las naciones. Barcos americanos han sido hundidos, vidas americanas tomadas, de maneras que nos han conmovido profundamente al conocerlas, pero los barcos y las personas de otras naciones neutrales y amigas han sido hundidos y abrumados en las aguas de la misma manera. No ha habido discriminación. El desafío es para toda la humanidad."

---
DOCUMENTO 3
Senador George Norris de Nebraska, Discurso Oponiéndose a la Declaración de Guerra de EE. UU., 4 de abril de 1917 — Registro del Congreso de EE. UU., dominio público:
"Vamos a la guerra por mandato del oro... Siento que estamos a punto de poner el signo del dólar en la bandera americana... Estoy convencido de que el objetivo del Presidente, al pedir la guerra, es servir a los intereses adinerados de nuestro país y no al pueblo común... Creo que deberíamos esperar pacientemente hasta que el pueblo americano esté dispuesto a ir a la guerra por su país en lugar de por los banqueros."
items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring (6/6) response argues a nuanced thesis — such as: 'U.S. entry into WWI resulted from both German provocation and American self-entanglement: the Zimmermann Telegram and unrestricted submarine warfare were genuine provocations, but Norris's dissent reveals that U.S. economic ties to the Allies had already compromised true neutrality — meaning American choices from 1914–1916 made some form of entry nearly inevitable by 1917.' SOAPS analysis for at least two documents: Document 1 (Zimmermann Telegram) — Speaker: Arthur Zimmermann, German Foreign Secretary; Occasion: Germany's planned resumption of unrestricted submarine warfare; Audience: German ambassador to Mexico, then intended for Mexican President Carranza; Purpose: secure Mexican alliance in the event of U.S. entry, create a North American distraction for the U.S.; Significance: its interception and publication (March 1, 1917) was the single greatest public catalyst for American war sentiment, because it made the threat to U.S. territorial security explicit. Document 3 (Norris) — Speaker: progressive Republican Senator from Nebraska; Occasion: Senate vote on war declaration; Audience: Senate and the American public; Purpose: oppose entry by arguing that Wall Street's financial interest in Allied victory was the real driver; Significance: Norris was one of only six senators to vote against war; his argument predicted later revisionist interpretations (Nye Committee, 1934). Cross-document synthesis: Documents 1 and 2 support the 'foreign provocation' thesis; Document 3 complicates it by arguing the U.S. was never truly neutral. Outside knowledge: U.S. loans to Allies (~$2.3 billion), J.P. Morgan as Allied purchasing agent, Lusitania (1915), Sussex Pledge (1916) and its violation, Wilson's 1916 re-election on peace platform, declaration April 6, 1917 (82–6 Senate, 373–50 House).

Document-Based Question: Peacemaking and Its Consequences — The Treaty of Versailles and the Fourteen Points, 1918–1919

Directions: Read the three documents below. Then write a well-organized essay addressing the following question: To what extent did the Treaty of Versailles fulfill, compromise, or betray Wilson's Fourteen Points, and what were the consequences of those compromises for world peace?

Your essay must:
— Apply HIPP or SOAPS analysis to at least two documents
— Use all three documents as evidence
— Incorporate outside knowledge of the Paris Peace Conference and subsequent events
— Construct a clear, defensible argument

---
DOCUMENT 1
President Woodrow Wilson, Fourteen Points Address to Congress, January 8, 1918 — Bryan, William Jennings, ed., Republic or Empire (1899), public domain, public domain (Points I, V, XIV selected):
"I. Open covenants of peace, openly arrived at, after which there shall be no private international understandings of any kind... V. A free, open-minded, and absolutely impartial adjustment of all colonial claims... XIV. A general association of nations must be formed under specific covenants for the purpose of affording mutual guarantees of political independence and territorial integrity to great and small states alike."

---
DOCUMENT 2
Treaty of Versailles, Article 231 ('War Guilt Clause'), June 28, 1919 — Avalon Project, Yale Law School, public domain:
"Germany accepts the responsibility of Germany and her allies for causing all the loss and damage to which the Allied and Associated Governments and their nationals have been subjected as a consequence of the war imposed upon them by the aggression of Germany and her allies."

---
DOCUMENT 3
Senator Henry Cabot Lodge, Speech on the Treaty of Versailles and Article X of the League Covenant, August 12, 1919 — Bryan, William Jennings, ed., Republic or Empire (1899), public domain, public domain:
"I have always loved but one flag... but I have loved America with an undivided heart, and I cannot share that devotion, cannot give affection to the mongrel banner invented for a league... I have loved but one flag and I am not prepared to put American boys under the command of some foreign general, or to bind America to go to war at the behest of other nations without the consent of Congress... Article X I consider the most dangerous obligation that has ever been submitted to the Senate."

items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring (6/6) response argues a nuanced thesis — such as: 'The Treaty of Versailles fundamentally betrayed Wilson's Fourteen Points by imposing punitive terms on Germany through the War Guilt Clause (Article 231), ignoring the principle of self-determination for colonial peoples, and then being rejected by the U.S. Senate, leaving the League of Nations fatally weakened — a combination of betrayals that created the conditions for the rise of fascism and World War II.' HIPP/SOAPS analysis: Document 1 (Wilson's Fourteen Points) — Historical context: U.S. entry into WWI needed justification beyond self-interest; Allied morale was flagging in January 1918 after Russia's exit; Intended audience: Congress, the American public, Allied governments, and — crucially — the German people and occupied territories (to offer an honorable peace alternative to continued war); Purpose: articulate a liberal internationalist peace framework that would justify U.S. sacrifice and build a post-war order; Point of view: idealistic liberal internationalism; note self-determination, open diplomacy, and collective security as the three pillars. Document 2 (War Guilt Clause) — Historical context: Paris Peace Conference (January–June 1919), with France (Clemenceau) and Britain (Lloyd George) demanding punishment and reparations; Intended audience: Germany and the German people, plus domestic Allied audiences; Purpose: establish the legal and moral basis for reparations ($33 billion ultimately assessed); Point of view: Allied governments determined to punish Germany; note how this directly contradicts Wilson's Point I (open covenants) and his vision of a 'peace without victory' (1917). Document 3 (Lodge) — Historical context: Senate ratification debate; Occasion: Lodge's effort to attach reservations, particularly to Article X; Audience: U.S. Senate and public; Purpose: defeat or reservationally modify the treaty to preserve congressional war powers and U.S. sovereignty; Point of view: Republican nationalist — Lodge opposed not the idea of a league per se but Article X's automatic obligation to defend members. Cross-document synthesis: Wilson promised an open, non-punitive peace (Doc 1); the Treaty imposed a punitive peace (Doc 2); and Lodge's nationalism ensured the U.S. would not be in the League (Doc 3) — three distinct failures compounding each other. Outside knowledge: Germany's resentment of the War Guilt Clause as a cause of the Weimar Republic's instability; $33 billion reparations burden; territorial losses (Rhineland occupation, Alsace-Lorraine, Polish Corridor); Hitler's rise using the 'stab in the back' myth and the 'war guilt lie'; League's failure to deter aggression in the 1930s.

Extended Response: World War I and the Transformation of American Society

Using your knowledge of U.S. history, write an extended essay that evaluates the following question: How did American participation in World War I transform American society, politics, and the United States' role in the world between 1917 and 1920, and to what extent did those transformations represent a permanent change versus a temporary wartime disruption?

Your essay must address at least three of the following dimensions: civil liberties and political dissent; the African American Great Migration and its causes; women's suffrage; organized labor and the economy; immigration and nativism; and U.S. foreign policy after the war. Your argument must draw specific connections between the wartime experiences of Americans on the home front and the political and social developments of the early 1920s.

Note: This question invites you to consider the experience of Tennessee soldiers in World War I. If you choose to address the experience of American soldiers on the Western Front, consider the role of Sergeant Alvin C. York of Pall Mall, Tennessee, whose October 8, 1918 action in the Argonne Forest — single-handedly killing 28 German soldiers and capturing 132 others while under heavy fire — became the most celebrated act of American individual heroism in the war and was used extensively in home-front propaganda and bond drives. York's story also illustrates the participation of rural, working-class, and religiously devout Americans in a war that many of them had initially opposed.

Using your knowledge of U.S. history, write an extended essay that evaluates the following question: What do the debates over American neutrality from 1914 to 1917 reveal about deep and enduring tensions in U.S. foreign policy between international engagement and isolationism, and how did the failure of the post-WWI peace settlement reinforce isolationist sentiment in the 1920s and 1930s?

UU. entre el compromiso internacional y el aislacionismo, y cómo reforzó el fracaso del acuerdo de paz posterior a la Primera Guerra Mundial el sentimiento aislacionista en los años 1920 y 1930?

items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring (4/4) response makes a complex, defensible claim — such as: 'The repeated failures of American internationalism — from Wilson's inability to keep the U.S. neutral without becoming economically entangled, to the Senate's rejection of the League of Nations, to the Neutrality Acts of the 1930s — reveal that American foreign policy in this era was characterized by a persistent gap between global ambitions and domestic political constraints, and that each failed attempt at internationalism deepened the isolationist reaction that followed.' At least three specific examples spanning WWI neutrality to the 1930s: (1) WWI neutrality failure — U.S. declared neutrality in 1914 but extended massive loans to the Allies; by 1917, $2.3 billion in Allied loans vs. $27 million in German loans meant the U.S. had a financial stake in an Allied victory that made true neutrality impossible; the Zimmermann Telegram and unrestricted submarine warfare then provided the final trigger. (2) League of Nations rejection (1919–1920) — Wilson's idealism at Paris was already compromised by Allied demands (War Guilt Clause, reparations); Lodge's reservations, especially Article X, reflected genuine constitutional concerns about congressional war powers; Wilson's refusal to compromise led to two Senate defeats; the resulting U.S. absence from the League fatally weakened collective security. (3) Neutrality Acts of the 1930s — Congress passed Neutrality Acts in 1935, 1936, and 1937, banning arms sales and loans to belligerents in any foreign war; these acts were directly caused by the Nye Committee findings (1934–36) that munitions makers ('merchants of death') and bankers had pushed the U.S. into WWI; the acts effectively prevented the U.S. from aiding Britain and France as Hitler remilitarized — showing how WWI's legacy of perceived manipulation drove isolationism to self-defeating extremes. Idealism vs. realism evaluation: Wilson's idealism (Fourteen Points, League) was genuine but politically naive — he underestimated Lodge's constitutional objections and his own deteriorating health; Lodge's realism was not pure isolationism but a demand for reservations that would have preserved U.S. sovereignty; the tragedy is that Wilson's and Lodge's positions were not as far apart as their personal conflict made them appear.
